test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: As per Mendel’s experiments with pea plants, tallness was called a ‘dominant’ trait compared to shortness because ________.

options.text: a plant was tall regardless of whether it had one gene (allele) or two genes (alleles) for tallness
in all organisms, including peas, tall individuals are more common than short individuals
the symbol for the gene for tallness was ‘T’, while the symbol for the gene for shortness was ‘t'
tall plants are larger in size than short plants

solution:
The correct answer is__** a plant was tall regardless of whether it had one gene (allele) or two genes (alleles) for tallness.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **hybrid offspring **generated will only acquire the **dominant characteristic **in the **phenotype**, in accordance with Mendel's first law of inheritance or law of dominance.
 
• **Recessive traits **are those that are **suppressed**, whereas **dominant traits **are those that **control **a **trait**.
 
• Tallness is the dominant characteristic.
 
• Because **tallness **is the **dominating characteristic**, a cross between a tall plant (TT) and a short pea plant (tt) produced only **tall plants.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Mendel researched the **inheritance **of peas' **height, flower colour, seed colour, **and **seed shape,** among other seven other traits.
 
• For example, he initially established pea lines with **tall vs. short height **as two different versions of a feature.
 
• He **bred **these lines to each other and watched to see how the **traits **were **passed down**.
 
• He had grown these lines for generations until they were **purebred**, or always produced **offspring **that were **identical **to the parent.
 
• Mendel counted the precise number of plants that displayed **each feature **in addition to noting how the plants appeared in each **generation**.
 
• Surprisingly, he discovered **fairly similar inheritance patterns **for all **seven traits **he examined.
